supported_claims.text: 働 is a Japanese-created character meaning “work,” read hataraku. It combines the person component 亻 with 動, “move.” 動 also links it with the reading dō. The construction is more informative than “a person moving”: it connects a human activity with an existing character used for movement.
亻 supplies a human meaning component, while 動 is associated with both movement and pronunciation. Whether the combined meaning directly motivated the coinage is disputed.

disagreements.text: The disagreement concerns the circumstances of formation, not whether 亻 and 動 are present. A person in motion remains an intelligible meaning association, but should not be presented as a settled reconstruction of the original coinage.

limitations.text: The exact coinage sequence remains disputed between a semantic combination account and differentiation of an existing written use; secondary citations do not establish the original inventor or date.
